about.title: Dana Point Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Dana Point residents rely on all kinds of consumer goods, vehicle parts, marine equipment and household products every day, and most of the time they work as intended. But when a manufacturing flaw, a poor design, or a missing warning label turns an ordinary product into a hazard, the results can be serious. Whether the incident happened at home near Stonehill Drive, out on the water, or while driving along Pacific Coast Highway or I-5, a defective product injury raises real questions about who made the item, who sold it, and what went wrong. California law gives injured consumers a path to hold manufacturers, distributors, and retailers accountable without having to prove negligence in many cases. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we simply connect you, free of charge, with an independent attorney in our network who can evaluate what happened and explain your options going forward.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About a Defective Product

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Case
items.desc: California generally allows injured consumers to pursue a claim by showing the product was defective and caused harm, without having to prove the manufacturer was careless.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable, which means an attorney can look at every link in the supply chain, not just one company.

items.title: Evidence Preservation Matters Early On
items.desc: Because the product itself is often the central piece of evidence, an attorney can advise you on how to keep it intact and unaltered before it's lost, repaired, or discarded.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Under California's strict liability approach, you typically need to show the product had a defect and that the defect caused your injury, rather than proving the company acted carelessly. An independent attorney can review your situation to explain which legal theory fits best.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Try to keep the product exactly as it was at the time of the incident, including packaging, parts, and any receipts. Don't attempt repairs or throw it away, since it's often the most important piece of evidence in a product liability claim.

items.question: Does it matter that this happened in Dana Point specifically?
items.answer: Local details can matter — for example, if the injury happened along a corridor like Pacific Coast Highway or Stonehill Drive, or involved marine gear near the harbor, those specifics can shape how a claim is investigated. An attorney familiar with Orange County can factor in local circumstances when evaluating your case.

items.question: Is there a cost to get connected with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, and attorneys in our network typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
